subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact private/ephemeral session contract should OpenClaw expose, and which storage, memory, plugin, channel, artifact, diagnostic, and UI surfaces must enforce it before the product can claim Private Mode?
rationale: The requested behavior is a privacy/security boundary rather than a narrow bug fix; automation cannot safely choose the threat model, user-facing semantics, or plugin/API compatibility contract.

options.title: Design a shared core contract
options.body: Define one additive private-session marker in the Gateway/session model, route it through plugins and UI, and block durable transcript, memory, compaction, artifact, and history writes for marked sessions before shipping the toggle.

options.title: Narrow to context suppression only
options.body: Ship only a demo-focused context-injection toggle, but explicitly avoid calling it Private Mode because it would not guarantee no persistence.

options.title: Defer or reject the feature
options.body: Close the feature direction and document existing mitigations such as contextInjection, pruning, and manual cleanup as non-private-mode alternatives.

recommendation.title: Design a shared core contract
recommendation.body: Define one additive private-session marker in the Gateway/session model, route it through plugins and UI, and block durable transcript, memory, compaction, artifact, and history writes for marked sessions before shipping the toggle.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior canonical review and recent memory/session ownership history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the security/product decision.
